dialect.guess: Micro Focus or similar (likely GnuCOBOL / OpenCOBOL, given the ORCA/JMA open-source medical context)
evidence: LINKAGE SECTION with USING clause on PROCEDURE DIVISION

purpose.summary: This program (ORCGM97) is part of the JMA (Japan Medical Association) open-source medical receipt software 'ORCA'. It manages a program-update screen (M97), handling online/offline update modes, job management, screen navigation, and shell-script invocation for applying software upgrades.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical receipt system)

notable_features: Japanese-language comments encoded in Latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, decoded as Latin-1 — garbled multibyte characters visible)
Screen-driven UI via MCP (Message Control Program) subsystem with CALL 'MCPSUB'
Shell script invocation via CALL 'ORCSMKPASS' and MCP-FUNC 'SHELL'
Multiple COPY statements for shared include files (CPPGKANRI.INC, CPJOBKANRI.INC, etc.)
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple COPY-based areas (MCPAREA, ORCA-SPA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA)
OCCURS 99 for list data in SPA
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — uses proprietary MCP database access layer
verdict.notes: The file is genuine COBOL source from the JMA ORCA medical receipt system (circa 2004 based on comment dates). Japanese comments are stored in a multibyte encoding (likely EUC-JP) but were decoded as Latin-1, producing garbled text. The program uses a proprietary screen/MCP framework rather than CICS, but the structure and event-driven pattern are analogous to online CICS programs. No COMP-3 usage detected despite being a business application, which is slightly unusual but not disqualifying.
